question.text: Per Chapter 9, private-credit yields in India tended to be high till 2023 and then moderated in 2024. The PRIMARY reason for moderation was:

answer.text: RBI imposing a ceiling on private-credit yields.
SEBI capping Cat II AIF coupon at 10%.
Entry of more AIF debt funds and other private lenders — increased supply of capital lowered the yield premium.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'In India, the yields in private credit tended to be high till 2023 when lenders were few but they moderated in 2024 with the entry of more AIF debt funds and other private lenders.' Supply-side expansion compressed spreads. The Trap: Options A and B invent yield caps. Option D (Section 115UB pass-through) doesn't affect yields at borrower level directly. Cross-Exam Context: XV uses private-credit yield trends. XIX-A covers market context. Manager's Pro-Tip: As the supply side grows, shift the portfolio mix toward more complex structures (acquisition financing, sub-ordinated LBO financing, promoter-share collateralised loans) — these still command premium yields due to structural complexity and are less commoditised.
